title: GitHub Pages Deployments That Stop Being Confusing

cover.alt: Asset tiles follow a folded route through a nested project doorway while a root-level route misses the entrance.

figures.title: Two ways to publish the same kind of artifact
figures.summary: Both approaches deliver static files; the configured source and handoff differ.

items.label: Publish source
items.detail: Branch approach: a selected branch. Actions approach: a workflow artifact.

items.label: Handoff
items.detail: Branch approach: push the output folder. Actions approach: upload the output folder as a Pages artifact.

items.label: Settings
items.detail: Choose the Pages source that matches the approach being used.

items.label: Output
items.detail: In both approaches, publish the directory containing the intended entry HTML and assets.

figures.caption: A comparison of the two deployment approaches in this article, not a claim that every Pages site uses a repository subpath.

figures.title: Trace a missing asset before republishing
figures.summary: Check the deployed paths and artifact instead of assuming a successful job proves the page works.

items.label: Base path
items.detail: Inspect generated asset URLs for the location where this site is served.

items.label: Output folder
items.detail: Confirm the chosen build folder contains the expected entry HTML.

items.label: Pages source
items.detail: Confirm repository settings match branch or Actions deployment.

items.label: Live request
items.detail: Open the live URL and inspect failed CSS or JavaScript requests.

items.label: Workflow log
items.detail: Inspect upload and deployment steps when the published output is wrong.
